responsibilities: Own and evolve our core dbt services - maintain CI/CD infrastructure, drive performance improvements, enforce quality standards, and support a large community of data practitioners building on top of it
Be the engineering interface for the analytics engineering community - unblock practitioners, review and improve shared patterns, and raise the bar on project quality, model structure, and SQL craft
Improve data quality and governance infrastructure - contribute to services covering anomaly detection, freshness monitoring, drift detection, and data contract enforcement
Shape data governance practices - drive standards around data ownership, data product thinking, and contract-first design across the data mesh
Contribute to our Python based tooling - feature extensions, integrations, and observability utilities; write well-tested, maintainable Python that practitioners can build on
Stay close to the platform - collaborate with our data platform team on the direction of shared infrastructure, representing the analytics perspective in technical decisions

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: its CI/CD pipelines, runtime configuration, data quality standards, and the tooling that keeps a broad community of data producers, analytics engineers, data analysts, and data scientists productive
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Quality, CI/CD, contracts and standards run through every responsibility, with no speed or shipping language to offset them.
evidence.domain_risk: N26 has reimagined banking for today's digital world.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: A licensed bank's core data warehouse — errors reach regulated financial reporting and a public-facing banking product at scale.
evidence.collaboration_width: data producers; analytics engineers; data analysts; data scientists; data platform team
evidence.data_team_maturity: The Analytics Engineering & Governance Enablement (AEGE) team is part of N26's wider Analytics Engineering & Data Governance (AEDG) function.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Named sub-teams with distinct charters inside a wider function, plus "large, multi-team dbt projects" and a data mesh, is a mature organisation.
evidence.jd_authorship: dbt at scale - macros, hooks, incremental models, project structure, CI/CD integration
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The bullets name specific dbt internals and named services — anomaly detection, freshness monitoring, drift detection — not generic stakeholder work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Be the engineering interface for the analytics engineering community - unblock practitioners
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The customers are the data function itself: practitioners building on the dbt services this role owns.
evidence.autonomy_level: Shape data governance practices - drive standards around data ownership, data product thinking, and contract-first design across the data mesh
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role sets organisation-wide standards — "shape", "drive standards", "own and evolve" — rather than delivering scoped work.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: Neither AI coding tools nor AI-consuming data products appear anywhere in the posting.
evidence.testing_framing: Improve data quality and governance infrastructure - contribute to services covering anomaly detection, freshness monitoring, drift detection, and data contract enforcement
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality and contract enforcement are the role's own infrastructure to own and improve, not tools listed in a skills section.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: the tooling that keeps a broad community of data producers, analytics engineers, data analysts, and data scientists productive
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The opening framing is trust — "ship trusted data products", quality standards, contract enforcement — so the fear is bad data spreading across the mesh.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Own and evolve our core dbt services - maintain CI/CD infrastructure, drive performance improvements
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Every infrastructure verb is maintain, evolve or improve against services that already exist.
evidence.loss_aversion: "We build the standards and tooling that the broader analytics engineering community depends on, to ship trusted data products" — trust in data products is the stated purpose of the team.
